newsitem.title: USA: Northrop signs $1.9 billion deal with McDonnell.
newsitem.headline: Northrop signs $1.9 billion deal with McDonnell.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp. said Monday it signed a $1.9 billion contract with McDonnell Douglas Corp. to make components for 80 McDonnell C-17 military transport aircraft over six years.
The deal follows a new agreement between the Air Force and McDonnell Douglas to build an additional 80 C-17s by 2004.

The company said the aircraft, the U.S. Air Force/McDonnell Douglas C-17 Globemaster III, is designed to carry large combat equipment and troops or humanitarian aid directly to small airfields anywhere in the world.
Last week, aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp. announced plans to acquire Los Angeles-based Northrop Grumman in a deal worth $11.6 billion.
The Lockheed-Northrop union, the latest in a series of blockbuster defence industry mergers, is expected to be completed by the end of the year pending approval by shareholders and regulators.
Northrop Grumman's commercial aircraft division produces engine housing, tail sections and other components at sites in Dallas, Georgia, and Florida.
The 80 C-17 aircraft will bring the Air Force's total Globemaster III fleet to 120.
Northrop stock rose $1.75 to $111.75 on the New York Stock Exchange, while McDonnell Douglas added about 56 cents to $70.75.
